title: Forward liquidity canvas: headcount & price tradeoffs
content:
PURPOSE:
Quick working model and narrative canvas to evaluate short-term liquidity sensitivity when we (1) re-prioritize hires across Eng/Infra/CS, (2) tune hosted pricing by feature, and (3) accelerate quantization/optimization adoption. Intended for finance+product+eng alignment; not finalized.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (TL;DR):
- Immediate runway uplift of ~6–10 weeks in the downside scenario if we (A) defer 12 lateral IC hires (avg fully-burdened $160k/yr) and (B) enact a 7% uplift in generation price for new high-throughput customers. 
- Upside scenario (aggressive quantization + volume pick-up) improves unit margin by ~13% and reduces required reserved GPU spend by ~$320k/quarter.
- Key hinge: token mix shift toward embeddings-heavy customers (lower per-unit revenue) can erode benefits unless we implement per-embedding surcharge or minimum monthly commit.

SCOPE AND QUESTIONS WE'RE ANSWERING:
1) If we pause non-critical hiring for 12 weeks, which teams give the best leverage on run-rate reduction vs product risk?
2) How sensitive is runway to small pricing moves (±5–10%) across three buckets: generation, embeddings, and dedicated capacity?
3) How much runway/ops-cost do we reclaim by fast-tracking our quantized model program (Q2 pilot -> Q4 production)?

ASSUMPTIONS (working):
- Currency: USD.
- Current cash runway baseline: 18 months at current burn (pre-adjustment).
- Average fully-burdened headcount cost (engineering): $160,000/year; SRE/infra hires: $185,000/year; CS/solutions hires: $140,000/year.
- Contract/consultant equivalent cost multiplier for short-term swaps: 1.6x of hourly-equivalent pro-rated cost.
- GPU reserved cost per quarter baseline: $1.6M across regions; spot/elastic strategies can reduce variable spend by 10–25% depending on availability.
- Token mix baseline: generation 62%, embeddings 30%, reranking/others 8%.
- Quantization adoption reduces per-token GPU runtime by 22% on average (lower bound 12%, upper 35% depending on model family).
- Price elasticity: small moves have non-linear effects; baseline elasticities used: generation e=-0.45, embeddings e=-0.7, dedicated capacity e=-0.15.

MODEL LAYOUT (spreadsheet tabs referenced):
- Tab: Summary (sensitivity matrix)
- Tab: Headcount Swap Deck (role buckets, risk scoring)
- Tab: Pricing Shock Matrix (per-bucket impact to ARR and churn)
- Tab: Quantization Runbook (capex, infra lift, forecasted token-cost delta)
- Tab: Action Tracker

HEADCOUNT TRADEOFF FRAMEWORK (short list):
- Non-critical ICs (low product dependency): pause 8 hires -> immediate run-rate saving: $106k/month. Risk: product velocity hit moderate.
- Platform/SRE hires: pause 4 hires -> saving: $61k/month. Risk: reliability and on-call capacity (high).
- Customer success / solutions hires: defer 6 hires -> saving: $70k/month. Risk: enterprise onboarding backlog increases (medium-high).
- Option: role-swap (delay hiring senior infra, hire contractors for short-term runbooks). Net delta over 6 months: +$45k cost but saves hiring headcount commitments.

PRICING SENSITIVITY HIGHLIGHTS:
- Small price uplift for generation (~7% on new customers only, partial grandfathering) -> modeled ARR +1.9% in 12 months, churn negligible in PLG funnel.
- Embeddings price changes are sensitive: +10% uplift -> modeled revenue +6% but adoption friction likely; elasticity high (e=-0.7) driven by customers optimizing embeddings frequency.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved) discount reduction (shrink discount by 2ppt) -> immediate yield +0.8% revenue; enterprise churn risk small but renewal conversations required.
- Recommendation: A layered rollout: 1) introduce feature-based surcharge (high-throughput generation >X tokens/min) 2) embed an embedding-volume breakpoint with stepped pricing 3) keep headline generation price stable for existing customers for 6mo.

SCENARIO SUMMARY (quarterly impact on runway / cash burn):
- Base: no change. runway = 18 months.
- Downside (decelerate hiring + price uplift): pause 12 hires (mix of IC/SRE/CS) + generation price +7% on new customers -> burn reduction $237k/month -> runway extends by ~8 weeks.
- Upside (quantization + spot GPU + small price tiering): quantization acceleration + spot mixing reduces GPU spend by $320k/quarter and per-token ops cost by 13% -> net burn reduction $140k/month -> runway extends by ~11 weeks; ARR improves as unit margin improves.

QUANTIZATION & INFRA INVESTMENT TRADEOFFS:
- One-time infra engineering uplift to shave integration friction: ~3 FTEs for 8 weeks (contractor/ops) = $90k one-time; benefit: recurring OpEx reduction on GPU costs.
- Break-even timeline: if quantization reduces GPU run-cost by >=15% sustained, payback in < 9 months.

RISKS & MITIGATIONS:
- Concentrated customer outcomes: if top-10 customers shift token mix to embeddings, revenue per token drops -> mitigation: negotiated committed minimums or per-embedding surcharge.
- Reliability impacts from pausing SRE hires -> mitigation: invest in runbook automation (one-time cost) and temporary contractor surge for on-call handoffs.
- Churn sensitivity from embedding price bumps -> mitigation: phased notices, opt-in experimental pricing for new customers only, and volume credits.

ACTIONS PROPOSED (near-term):
1) Freeze non-critical IC hiring for 12 weeks; finance to re-forecast weekly and report to Exec. Owner: Rajiv. Due: 2026-12-10.
2) Implement a small experimental generation surcharge on new high-throughput accounts (feature-tier enablement) and monitor adoption for 60 days. Owner: Product-hosted-api. Due: 2026-12-22.
3) Kick a quantization pilot (one pre-prod shard) with dedicated infra support; finance to provision $90k one-time budget. Owner: Applied-ML. Due: 2027-01-15.
4) Build a short negotiation playbook for enterprise renewals where embedding-heavy usage is identified. Owner: GTM. Due: 2027-01-05.

OPEN QUESTIONS (for next working session):
- If we enact a 5% embedding price increase for new customers, what is the forecasted churn vs. ARR gain after 6 months (more granular cohort modeling needed)?
- If we shift 20% of reserved GPU capacity to spot with auto-fallback, what are credible availability scenarios by region? (SRE/Infra input needed).
- How many enterprise deals would need to be re-structured to protect unit margin if token mix shifts? run a top-20 account sensitivity.

NOTES / LINKS: 
- See pricing shock matrix tab for sensitivity tables and cell-level formulas (referenced Google Sheet).
- Confluence draft: Forward Liquidity Canvas (link above) has background slides and meeting notes.
- Related tickets: JIRA-ENG-7001 (quantization infra), JIRA-SALES-1892 (enterprise embedding deals).

APPENDIX: Quick math snippets (copyable)
- Monthly saving per paused hire = fully-burdened annual / 12. Example: $160k/12 = $13.3k/month per IC.
- Runway delta (months) = current_cash / (current_burn - monthly_savings).
- GPU quarterly saving example: $320k/quarter -> $106.7k/month.

WORKING CONCLUSIONS (for exec readout):
- Moderate, surgical hiring pauses + a narrowly scoped pricing experiment produce near-term runway relief with limited product risk if coupled with explicit mitigation actions.
- Quantization is the higher-payoff lever over 6–12 months but requires a small, targeted infra investment to avoid integration drag.
- We should prioritize: 1) freeze non-critical hiring 2) run a price experiment on new high-throughput generation customers 3) accelerate the quantization pilot with a fast decision gate.
